tb21_profile.skill: Filesystem/raw-storage forensics: find the residual bytes of an unlinked file (unallocated blocks, journal, open fds) and pull out a string matching a tight format constraint
tb21_profile.domain: Linux filesystem internals and digital forensics - ext4/raw images, carving, byte scanning, credential recovery
tb21_profile.task_form: recover-deleted-or-corrupted-data, then filter candidates against a hard pattern (23 chars, 8XD prefix, W54 suffix, [A-Z0-9] only)

verifier_notes: No grade disputed. security_20260606_172606_006 is graded `weak` but is the single most on-point instruction in the pool (a deleted password.txt inside a disk image); I kept it in final_top10 on content, noting the weak grade. tw_651283 and tw_286226 are FREE and stay in per_source only.

tools.py search rebench 'binary file|byte offset|struct\.unpack|hexdump|raw bytes|file signature|magic number|parse.*binary|zipfile|tarfile'
tools.py search smith 'zipfile|tarfile|byte offset|struct\.unpack|raw bytes|chardet|charset|encoding detect'

TMax-15K.reason: Recover a named deleted file (trace.log) from a raw ext4 image; the identical forensic mechanism this TB2.1 task needs.
Both halves at once: extract a fixed-length key with a known prefix (AUTHKEY-) and recover a deleted file from a raw logs-partition image.
Filesystem corruption deleted the telemetry log; recover it by name from a raw partition image of the drive.
Recover deleted crash.dat from an unmounted filesystem image - same unmounted-image scan, same by-name target.
Recover a deleted log from an ext4 image and pull an exact timestamp out of it: recovery plus constrained string extraction.
settings.bin was deleted; only a raw partition dump remains, so the content must be found in unallocated space.
Deleted-file recovery from an ext4 partition image as phase one of a pipeline repair; same forensic step, extra scaffolding.
The rm'd file is still held open by a running tail; recover through /proc/<pid>/fd - the other standard answer to 'file deleted, data still there'.
Forensic sweep of an attacker's ext4 evidence image to pull out a specific artefact; same image-scanning toolkit.
Phase 1 is recovering a log file deleted by a faulty rotation before the rest of the pipeline can be fixed.

Combines both halves: extract a fixed-length key with a known prefix, and recover a deleted file from a raw partition image.
Deleted telemetry log recovered by name from a raw partition image after filesystem corruption; strongly verified.
Recover credentials hidden somewhere on a disk image - recovery plus a targeted hunt for a secret string, both halves of this task.
Recover deleted crash.dat from an unmounted filesystem image; unmounted-image scanning is the core technique here.

notes: This TB2.1 task is unusually well served: TMax-15K and CalibForge each hold a dozen-plus raw-image deleted-file-recovery tasks, and the honest top 10 is entirely from those two pools. CalibForge is the clearest win for a new corpus here - its forensics/carving cluster is both large and well verified (several `strong`), and software-engineering_20260610_112157_014 plus security_20260606_172606_006 are closer than anything in the v1 pool except the TMax ext4 family. Terminal-Lego-15k is the weak new corpus for this task: it has no filesystem forensics at all, only password-policy and regex-validation exercises, so its ranks 5-10 are honest 2s. SWE-Rebench could not field 10 defensible candidates - ranks 5-10 are quota filler scored 1. SWE-Smith is only slightly better (byte-classification libraries like chardet/charset_normalizer). Recursive-Task-Synthesis offers only git-history recovery and steganography, which share the goal ('the deleted secret still exists somewhere') but not the storage-layer mechanism; all of it is `absent`, and graded equivalents exist in TMax and CalibForge, so none of it entered final_top10.
